2901: from κραταιός; to empower, i.e. (passively) increase in vigor:--be strengthened, be (wax) strong.
2902: from κράτος; to use strength, i.e. seize or retain (literally or figuratively):--hold (by, fast), keep, lay hand (hold) on, obtain, retain, take (by).
2903: superlative of a derivative of κράτος; strongest, i.e. (in dignity) very honorable:--most excellent (noble).
2904: perhaps a primary word; vigor ("great") (literally or figuratively):--dominion, might(-ily), power, strength.
2906: from κράζω; an outcry (in notification, tumult or grief):--clamour, cry(-ing).
2908: neuter of an alternate form of κρείττων; (as noun) better, i.e. greater advantage:--better.
2909: comparative of a derivative of κράτος; stronger, i.e. (figuratively) better, i.e. nobler:--best, better.
2910: a prolonged form of a primary verb; to hang:--hang.
2911: from κρεμάννυμι; overhanging, i.e. a precipice:--steep place.
2912: from Κρήτη; a Cretan, i.e. inhabitant of Crete:--Crete, Cretian.
2913: of Latin origin; growing; Cresces (i.e. Crescens), a Christian:--Crescens.
2914: of uncertain derivation; Crete, an island in the Mediterranean:--Crete.
2917: from κρίνω; a decision (the function or the effect, for or against ("crime")):--avenge, condemned, condemnation, damnation, + go to law, judgment.
2918: perhaps a prim word; a lily:--lily.
2919: properly, to distinguish, i.e. decide (mentally or judicially); by implication, to try, condemn, punish:--avenge, conclude, condemn, damn, decree, determine, esteem, judge, go to (sue at the) law, ordain, call in question, sentence to, think.
2921: of Latin origin; "crisp"; Crispus, a Corinthian:--Crispus.
2922: neuter of a presumed derivative of κριτής; a rule of judging ("criterion"), i.e. (by implication) a tribunal:--to judge, judgment (seat).
2923: from κρίνω; a judge (genitive case or specially):--judge.
2925: apparently a primary verb; to rap:--knock.
2926: feminine of κρυπτός; a hidden place, i.e. cellar ("crypt"):--secret.
2927: from κρύπτω; concealed, i.e. private:--hid(-den), inward(-ly), secret.
2928: a primary verb; to conceal (properly, by covering):--hide (self), keep secret, secret(-ly).
2929: from κρύσταλλος; to make (i.e. intransitively, resemble) ice ("crystallize"):--be clear as crystal.
2930: from a derivative of (frost); ice, i.e. (by analogy) rock "crystal":--crystal.
2932: a primary verb; to get, i.e. acquire (by any means; own):--obtain, possess, provide, purchase.
2933: from κτάομαι; an acquirement, i.e. estate:--possession.
2934: from κτάομαι; property, i.e. (specially) a domestic animal:--beast.
2936: probably akin to κτάομαι (through the idea of proprietorship of the manufacturer); to fabricate, i.e. found (form originally):--create, Creator, make.
2937: from κτίζω; original formation (properly, the act; by implication, the thing, literally or figuratively):--building, creation, creature, ordinance.
2938: from κτίζω; an original formation (concretely), i.e. product (created thing):--creature.
2939: from κτίζω; a founder, i.e. God (as author of all things):--Creator.
2940: from (a "cube", i.e. die for playing); gambling, i.e. (figuratively) artifice or fraud:--sleight.
2941: from (of Latin origin, to steer); pilotage, i.e. (figuratively) directorship (in the church):--government.
2942: from the same as κυβέρνησις; helmsman, i.e. (by implication) captain:--(ship) master.
2943: adverb from the same as κύκλῳ; from the circle, i.e. all around:--(round) about.
2944: from the same as κύκλῳ; to encircle, i.e. surround:--compass (about), come (stand) round about.
2945: as if dative case of (a ring, "cycle"; akin to κυλιόω); i.e. in a circle (by implication, of ἐν), i.e. (adverbially) all around:--round about.
2946: from κυλιόω; a wallow (the effect of rolling), i.e. filth:--wallowing.
2947: from the base of κῦμα (through the idea of circularity; compare κύκλῳ, εἱλίσσω); to roll about:--wallow.
2948: from the same as κυλιόω; rocking about, i.e. crippled (maimed, in feet or hands):--maimed.
2949: from (to swell (with young), i.e. bend, curve); a billow (as bursting or toppling):--wave.
2950: from a derivative of the base of κῦμα; a "cymbal" (as hollow):--cymbal.
2951: of foreign origin (compare כַּמֹּן); dill or fennel ("cummin"):--cummin.
2952: neuter of a presumed derivative of κύων; a puppy:--dog.
2953: from Κύπρος; a Cyprian (Cypriot), i.e. inhabitant of Cyprus:--of Cyprus.
2954: of uncertain origin; Cyprus, an island in the Mediterranean:--Cyprus.
2955: probably from the base of κῦμα; to bend forward:--stoop (down).
2956: from Κυρήνη; i.e. Cyrenæan, i.e. inhabitant of Cyrene:--of Cyrene, Cyrenian.
2957: of uncertain derivation; Cyrene, a region of Africa:--Cyrene.
2958: of Latin origin; Cyrenius (i.e. Quirinus), a Roman:--Cyrenius.
2959: feminine of κύριος; Cyria, a Christian woman:--lady.
2960: from κύριος; belonging to the Lord (Jehovah or Jesus):--Lord's.
2961: from κύριος; to rule:--have dominion over, lord, be lord of, exercise lordship over.
2962: from (supremacy); supreme in authority, i.e. (as noun) controller; by implication, Master (as a respectful title):-- God, Lord, master, Sir.
2963: from κύριος; mastery, i.e. (concretely and collectively) rulers:--dominion, government.
2964: from the same as κύριος; to make authoritative, i.e. ratify:--confirm.
2965: a primary word; a dog ("hound") (literally or figuratively):--dog.
2966: from the base of κολάζω; a limb of the body (as if lopped):--carcase.
2967: from the base of κολάζω; to estop, i.e. prevent (by word or act):--forbid, hinder, keep from, let, not suffer, withstand.
2968: from κεῖμαι; a hamlet (as if laid down):--town, village.
2969: from κώμη and πόλις; an unwalled city:--town.
2970: from κεῖμαι; a carousal (as if letting loose):--revelling, rioting.
2971: apparently a derivative of the base of κέντρον and a derivative of ὀπτάνομαι; a mosquito (from its stinging proboscis):--gnat.
2972: of uncertain origin; Cos, an island in the Mediterranean:--Cos.
2973: of Hebrew origin (compare קֶסֶם); Cosam (i.e. Kosam) an Israelite:--Cosam.
2974: from κόπτω; blunted, i.e. (figuratively) of hearing (deaf) or speech (dumb):--deaf, dumb, speechless.
2975: a prolonged form of a primary verb, which is only used as an alternate in certain tenses; to lot, i.e. determine (by implication, receive) especially by lot:--his lot be, cast lots, obtain.
2976: probably of Hebrew origin (אֶלְעָזָר); Lazarus (i.e. Elazar), the name of two Israelites (one imaginary):--Lazarus.
2978: of uncertain derivation; a whirlwind (squall):--storm, tempest.
2980: a prolonged form of an otherwise obsolete verb; to talk, i.e. utter words:--preach, say, speak (after), talk, tell, utter. Compare λέγω.
2982: of Hebrew origin (מָה with prepositional prefix); lama (i.e. why):--lama.
2983: a prolonged form of a primary verb, which is use only as an alternate in certain tenses; to take (in very many applications, literally and figuratively (properly objective or active, to get hold of; whereas δέχομαι is rather subjective or passive, to have offered to one; while αἱρέομαι is more violent, to seize or remove)):--accept, + be amazed, assay, attain, bring, X when I call, catch, come on (X unto), + forget, have, hold, obtain, receive (X after), take (away, up).
2984: of Hebrew origin (לֶמֶךְ); Lamech (i.e. Lemek), a patriarch:--Lamech.
2985: from λάμπω; a "lamp" or flambeau:--lamp, light, torch.
2986: from the same as λαμπάς; radiant; by analogy, limpid; figuratively, magnificent or sumptuous (in appearance):--bright, clear, gay, goodly, gorgeous, white.
2988: adverb from λαμπρός; brilliantly, i.e. figuratively, luxuriously:--sumptuously.
2989: a primary verb; to beam, i.e. radiate brilliancy (literally or figuratively):--give light, shine.
2990: a prolonged form of a primary verb, which is used only as an alternate in certain tenses; to lie hid (literally or figuratively); often used adverbially, unwittingly:--be hid, be ignorant of, unawares.
2991: from a compound of (a stone) and the base of ξηρός (in its original sense of scraping); rock-quarried:--hewn in stone.
2992: apparently a primary word; a people (in general; thus differing from δῆμος, which denotes one's own populace):--people.
2993: from a compound of λαός and δίκη; Laodicia, a place in Asia Minor:--Laodicea.
2994: from Λαοδίκεια; a Laodicean, i.e. inhabitant of Laodicia:--Laodicean.
2996: of uncertain origin; Lasæa, a place in Crete:--Lasea.
2997: a strengthened form of a primary verb, which only occurs in this and another prolonged form as alternate in certain tenses; to crack open (from a fall):--burst asunder.
2998: from the same as the first part of λαξευτός and the base of τομώτερος; to quarry:--hew.
2999: from λατρεύω; ministration of God, i.e. worship:--(divine) service.
